title: The integral scalar extension is well defined, a derived limit, and O_E-linear
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E\subset L$ finite extensions of $\Ql$ ($L$ finite over $\Ql$, $E$ a subfield of $L$ containing $\Ql$) [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ and finite coefficient rings $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $A_{L,m}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ ($m\geq1$). The restriction of $|\cdot|_L$ to $E$ is an absolute value extending $|\cdot|_\ell$, hence equals $|\cdot|_E$ [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value]; so $\mathcal O_E=\mathcal O_L\cap E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and $|\varpi_E|_L<1$, i.e. $\varpi_E\in\varpi_L\mathcal O_L$. Hence $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subset\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$, and the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ induces ring maps $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$ commuting with the transition maps $A_{E,m+1}\to A_{E,m}$, $A_{L,m+1}\to A_{L,m}$. Let $Y$ be a scheme with small pro-etale site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and for a ring $A$ let $A_Y$ be the constant sheaf of rings, functorial in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ let $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}=\varprojlim_m(A_{F,m})_Y$ be the completed coefficient sheaf with projections $\pi^F_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\to(A_{F,m})_Y$, restriction of scalars $\operatorname{Res}^F_m$ along $\pi^F_m$ and derived category $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_F)$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$-modules [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Put $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\circ\pi^E_m:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{L,m})_Y$; then $\rho_m$ is $\rho_{m+1}$ followed by $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$.

For a complex $P$ of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules put $P_{L,m}=P\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}}(A_{L,m})_Y$, the termwise change of rings along $\rho_m$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a complex of $(A_{L,m})_Y$-modules. The transition $(A_{L,m+1})_Y\to(A_{L,m})_Y$ induces a map of complexes $P_{L,m+1}\to P_{L,m}$; since $\pi^L_m$ is $\pi^L_{m+1}$ followed by that transition, it is a map $t_m:\operatorname{Res}^L_{m+1}P_{L,m+1}\to\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}$ of complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Write

$$
 \operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}=\operatorname{Cone}\Bigl(1-s:\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\to\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\Bigr)[-1],\qquad (c_m)_m\mapsto(c_m-t_m(c_{m+1}))_m,
$$

on the termwise countable products of sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$-modules [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. A K-flat complex is meant in the sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex] for the ringed site $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y})$.

Then:
1. If $u:P\to P'$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat complexes of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$-modules with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the induced maps $P_{L,m}\to P'_{L,m}$ are quasi-isomorphisms for every $m$, and the induced map $\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m}\to\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mP'_{L,m}$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
2. Consequently, choosing for every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ a quasi-isomorphism $P_K\to K$ with $P_K$ K-flat with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], $K\mapsto\operatorname{Rlim}^{\mathrm c}_m\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P_K)_{L,m}$ (on a morphism $K\to K'$, the map induced by the morphism $P_K\to P_{K'}$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ it determines) is a well-defined additive functor $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$, independent of the choice of the resolutions up to unique isomorphism of functors compatible with their natural comparison isomorphisms on K-flat representatives; it commutes with the shift; and each value is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ of the tower $(\operatorname{Res}^L_m(P_K)_{L,m},t_m)_m$.
3. The functor of (2) is $\mathcal O_E$-linear: for $a\in\mathcal O_E$ and a morphism $f$ of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ it sends $af$ to $a$ times the image of $f$, where $\mathcal O_E$ acts on the Hom groups of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and, through $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, of $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ by the constant global sections [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category].

source.place: Prop. 6.8.14 (1), p. 61 (the scalar-extension functors D_cons(X_proet,O_F) -> D_cons(X_proet,O_E) of the colimit, used without construction); Def. 3.4.10, p. 22, and Prop. 3.5.1 (3), p. 24 (completion as R lim of the reductions modulo powers of the ideal). The well-definedness argument is the one of dag node lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, for the ring maps rho_m in place of pi_m.

proof.text: Write $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,Y}$ and $B_m=(A_{L,m})_Y$. The absolute-value uniqueness in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] identifies the restriction from $L$ with that on $E$. By the definition of uniformizer in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $\varpi_E\in\mathfrak m_L=\varpi_L\mathcal O_L$, so $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subseteq\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$. Thus the quotient map sends the class of $a$ to its class modulo $\varpi_L^m$; reducing either before or after this map gives that same class. Functorial constant sheafification and the limit projections give the asserted compatible $\rho_m$. The transition on tensor generators is $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\bar b$; the equality $\rho_m=\mathrm{red}\circ\rho_{m+1}$ makes this balanced. Restricting along the projections from $S$ makes it $S$-linear. All identities descend from presheaf tensors to their sheafifications.

source.place: Termwise coefficient change preceding Tag 06YT; elementary quotient and tensor identities

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-change-of-rings-kflat-quasi-iso] on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to the sheaf-ring map $\rho_m:R\to B_m$. It gives that $u\otimes_R B_m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This needs no flatness of $B_m$ over $R$. Restriction of scalars in [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] preserves the underlying abelian sheaf, kernels, images and cokernels: these acquire the restricted action, so cohomology also has the same underlying sheaf and restriction preserves this quasi-isomorphism. The resulting maps $a_m$ commute strictly with transitions, since both orders send $x\otimes b$ to $u(x)\otimes\bar b$.

For any resulting tower $C_m=\operatorname{Res}^L_m P_{L,m}$ put $A=\prod_m C_m$ and $v=1-s$. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence] (2), this termwise product represents the derived-category product. The rotated cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for $v$ is a Roos triangle, so $T(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(v)[-1]$ is a derived limit in exactly the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. For the strict tower map of step 2, $g=\prod_m a_m$ satisfies $gv=v\prime g$. The diagonal map on the two cone summands gives a morphism of Roos triangles. All its level maps are isomorphisms in the derived category; [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] says that its cone map is an isomorphism. Applying every cohomology functor proves that $T(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, completing (1).

The generator formulas give additive functors on complexes; the induced cone map is diagonal, so identities, composition and sums are preserved. They also respect homotopies. If $u-u\prime=dh+hd$, coefficient change sends $h$ to $h_m=h\otimes 1$, which commutes with reduction. Put $h_A=\prod h_m$; it commutes with $v=1-s$. In the shifted-cone convention $d(b,a)=(-db-va,da)$, with $b\in A^{n-1}$ and $a\in A^n$, the degree $-1$ map $H(b,a)=(-h_A b,h_A a)$ satisfies $dH+Hd=(\prod(u_m-u\prime_m),\prod(u_m-u\prime_m))$: the cross terms are $h_Av-vh_A=0$. Thus $T$ induces an additive functor from the full homotopy subcategory of K-flat complexes with flat terms to $D(S)$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the localization of that full K-flat-with-flat-terms homotopy subcategory at its quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent to $D(R)$. The chosen skeleton of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] makes the site small in the larger universe required there. Step 3 proves that $T$ inverts these quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (1) and transport along the equivalence to obtain $F:D(R)\to D(S)$ with natural comparisons $F(QP)\cong QT(P)$. It is additive: the displayed construction carries the zero complex to zero and preserves the canonical inclusions and projections of finite biproducts. K-flat flat-term complexes are closed under finite biproducts (tensoring a finite sum with an acyclic complex is a finite sum of acyclic complexes). The biproduct equations are preserved after localization, and every object has a K-flat model, so $F$ preserves finite biproducts. The formula $f+g=\nabla(f\oplus g)\Delta$ then proves additivity.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; site K-flat localization following Tag 06YT

proof.text: Choose $q_K:P_K\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The comparison above and $F(Qq_K)^{-1}$ give $i_K:F(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}QT(P_K)$. Define the map assigned to $f:K\to K\prime$ to be $i_{K\prime}F(f)i_K^{-1}$. This defines the action meant by the statement without assuming a chain-map lift of every derived morphism. It preserves identities, composition and sums. A second choice gives the natural comparison $i\prime_K i_K^{-1}$. Its uniqueness is precisely uniqueness compatible with the K-flat comparisons, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (2), not unqualified uniqueness of natural isomorphisms. The derived-limit assertion for its values was proved in step 3.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), followed by Tag 06YT; Tag 04VG for comparison uniqueness

proof.text: The shift from [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves K-flatness and flat terms: tensoring with a shifted complex shifts the total tensor, hence preserves acyclicity. Coefficient change, restriction and termwise products commute with shift. For the cone convention of step 4, identify $T(P[1])^n=A^n\oplus A^{n+1}=T(P)[1]^n$ and use $(b,a)\mapsto(-b,a)$. The differential on the source is $(db-va,-da)$; on the target it is $(db+va,-da)$, so the formula is a chain isomorphism. It is natural in $P$. Localization uniqueness extends it to a natural $F\circ[1]\cong[1]\circ F$, which transports through the $i_K$ to the chosen-resolution functor.

source.place: Explicit shifted-cone signs in Tag 08TC, using the cochain shift convention

proof.text: Constant sections give $\mathcal O_E$-linear structures on both module-sheaf categories, on the target through $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$: sums and composition are bilinear sectionwise. By [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], these induce the asserted scalar actions on the derived categories and linear localization functors. For $a\in\mathcal O_E$, tensor balancing gives $(ax)\otimes b=x\otimes\iota_m(a)b$. Thus $T(a\,\mathrm{id}_P)=a\,\mathrm{id}_{T(P)}$, on both product and cone summands, since the $S$-action projects to $a\bmod\varpi_L^m$ in every coordinate. These are equal natural endomorphisms on K-flat representatives. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (3), their descended endomorphisms coincide on every object: $F(a\,\mathrm{id}_K)=a\,\mathrm{id}_{F(K)}$. Hence $F(af)=F((a\,\mathrm{id})f)=aF(f)$; conjugating by the $S$-linear $i_K$ preserves this equality. This proves (3) without imposing an unrelated characteristic $p$ or using the narrower constructible-linearity lemma.
